rationale: Cheap RF jamming of unprotected C2/MAVLink links reliably forces fail-safe or crashes of individual BVLOS flights within jammer range.
A JWT alg=none flaw, once found, gives repeatable and unrestricted authorisation that can put unvetted flights into managed airspace.
Vendor-level backdoors need a nation-state level of effort and are hard to detect, but they compromise the whole deployed fleet at once.
Physical sabotage requires on-site presence and is localised, but it can endanger UAM landings and passengers at the affected vertiport.
Tampering with regulator logs needs privileged access and mainly erodes oversight and accountability, with only indirect safety effects.
SQL injection is a well-known, easily scanned flaw; mass flight-plan corruption hits many operators and moderately degrades the safety picture.
Leaked strategic documents give adversaries reconnaissance value but have no direct safety consequence.
Malicious flight-controller firmware gives full control of the aircraft; exposed debug ports and unsigned updates are easy to spot but require access.
Injecting fake geofences through an unauthenticated feed can lead many UAS into restricted airspace, though other ATM safeguards may still intervene.
Phantom tracks and hidden real conflicts defeat separation monitoring, creating a direct risk of mid-air collision.
A stolen API key with no rate limits makes bulk exfiltration trivial, but the impact is mainly confidentiality rather than safety.
Poisoning the single source of truth corrupts every dependent U-Space service at once, a systemic and potentially catastrophic failure.
Weak identity proofing lets illegitimate operators fly, but the effect is limited to individual flights and accountability.
Deleting no-fly-zone records at the database level persistently opens protected airspace, such as around airports, to every consuming service.
Falsified weather and traffic feeds from unverified third parties can produce unsafe routing and UAS-to-UAS conflicts across a region.
Exploiting regulatory ambiguity is low-skill and repeatable, but it only weakens security posture rather than causing direct harm.
Civil GNSS is unauthenticated and public knowledge; cheap jammers and SDR spoofers can misdirect or blind every UAS in an area.
Log tampering hides incidents and hampers forensics after the fact but causes no direct operational or safety harm.
A ground power outage halts operations, while BMS manipulation can cause forced landings or in-flight power loss.
DDoS on a single gateway with no mitigation is trivial and blocks the whole volume, but flights mostly fail safe by not being authorised.
Signal injection into sensors or the IMU needs specialised, proximate attacks and affects few aircraft, but it can cause crashes.
